messages:
teo: FYI I hit a parity gap between TS and Python SDKs in the getting-started sample around auth failure handling.
rachel: what shape difference?
teo: TS surfaces a plain fetch error with message '401 Unauthorized'. Python raises a RefreshTokenError object with fields {type: 'Auth.RefreshNeeded', status: 401, retryable: true}.
vik: that's annoying for onboarding because the sample app shows naive retry loops that won't detect a refresh case in TS.
teo: repro in sample-app/auth-smoke: create a short-lived key (15s) and run the quickstart loop until expiry. TS just bubbles a string.
rachel: proposal: canonical client-side shape: type, status, subcode, retryable, user_message, raw_body. Keep type stable like 'Auth.RefreshNeeded' so code can do switch(e.type).
vik: add machine hints array too, e.g. ["refresh_token", "backoff:exp"], so libraries and apps can pick a strategy.
teo: ops caveat: 401 can mean malformed key vs expired token. Use subcodes from auth-service when available; otherwise SDK can synthesize 'expired'.
rachel: action items: 1) DEVEX ticket with schema + sample patches for TS/Python, 2) patch sample-app to show canonical detection and a friendly log message instead of raw 401, 3) unit test asserting SDK normalizes server error into the canonical shape.
vik: i'll own TS normalization adapter and tests, will keep change behind feature flag for compatibility.
sdk-bot: created DEVEX-5010: "Normalize auth error shapes across SDKs + update onboarding sample" (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex/issues/5010).
teo: thanks. Also suggest a tiny docs snippet under "Onboarding errors" that explains common error types and recommended actions.
rachel: will draft the snippet and add an e2e to the sample-app that simulates expired key so new devs can see the refresh flow.
vik: planning to open TS PR today with tests.
teo: great sync, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
